title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measures the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline), implemented as paired success-rate difference per the preregistration. Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations under original power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in the preregistered power calculation. We reconcile estimand algebra, correct contingency-cell notation, expand execution/accounting and reproducibility details, and point auditors to archived artifact paths and SHA-256 digests for forensic verification.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) offer an efficient interface for converting operator intent into device-specific network configuration. However, incorrect commands may cause outages or policy violations; consequently, production proposals commonly interpose deterministic validators and automated repair loops as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Despite that design intuition, rigorous, preregistered quantification of the marginal operational benefit from adding a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract (single hosted model, limited automated repairs) is rare and often lacks forensic artifact traceability. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? We designed a paired estimand to control task heterogeneity by comparing, within each task, the initial shared candidate (baseline) to the final guarded configuration (after deterministic validation and up to one automated repair). Key contribution: a fully preregistered, artifact-hashed, paired confirmatory run with deterministic validator traces and complete provider-call accounting for forensic auditors.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification (header-space analysis, incremental checkers) and runtime validators (e.g., VeriFlow) provide established pre-deployment safety methods. Recent LLM→NetOps work evaluates intent-driven config generation, but typically reports leaderboards or single-condition accuracies without preregistration or end-to-end validator traces. NetConfEval and other NetOps LLM evaluations examine LLM correctness but seldom quantify the marginal benefit of deterministically verifying a fixed LLM candidate under an explicit adapter contract. Our study differs by (1) holding the initial LLM candidate constant (shared_initial generation), (2) using a deterministic validator that produces canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks, (3) bounding repair attempts (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1), and (4) publishing cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts so that auditors can reconstruct contingency tables and per-episode traces.
sections.methodology:
Design and preregistration. We preregistered a paired binary design (N=200 intent→configuration tasks) and defined the primary_estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = not actionable-error). The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test; we also prespecified a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistration contains the complete sampling plan, stratified task-bank templates (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66, Juniper-like N=67, RFC‑neutral N=67), adapter contract, retry and missingness rules, and multiplicity plan (single primary hypothesis). The preregistration SHA-256 is archived above.

Adapter contract, model, and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) so each task supplied a single initial candidate reused across baseline and guarded conditions. The adapter allowed at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1); provider-call accounting is recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...); host-model call events = 201 with stage_counts {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}, matching model_calls_used = 201 in the execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). These artifact hashes are authoritative and archived.

Synthetic task bank, validator, and scoring. We used a deterministic synthetic multi-vendor intent bank generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), permitted touched fields, and an explicit required_sequence. A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses responses into canonical ASTs, enforces syntactic/vendor parse rules, intent-constraint checks, dependency/workflow policies, and simulator-backed semantic checks; the validator emits per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) and a binary score ∈ {0,1} using scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ are the authoritative record. Representative scoring examples and their SHA-256 digests are archived in the evidence bundle.

Execution, retries, and missingness. The preregistered retry policy attempted up to two automatic retries on provider-call failures; if unresolved such episodes are excluded from the primary paired analysis per the missingness plan. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution manifest: planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions), completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200 (execution manifest and analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00...). All provider calls, retries (none), and stage counts are logged and hashed for reproducibility.

Statistical analysis. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and produced (a) contingency table n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00, (b) exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and (c) paired bootstrap percentile CI for the absolute paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). All analysis CSVs and logs are archived and hashed (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...). We preserved the preregistered multiplicity policy: one primary confirmatory hypothesis and labeled secondary/exploratory tests.
sections.results:
Primary paired outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Contingency-cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199 (guarded=1 & baseline=1), n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0; a guarded-only improvement), n_01 = 0 (guarded=0 & baseline=1), n_00 = 0 (both invalid). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI for absolute paired difference = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729).

Estimand and hypothesis reconciliation. The preregistered primary_estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; the preregistered textual hypothesis stated a ≥50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate. Algebraic mapping: actionable_error_rate = 1 − success_rate, so a relative reduction r in actionable-error rate corresponds to guarded_success − baseline_success = r·(baseline_error) / ??? (careful: relative reductions on a very small baseline produce tiny absolute differences). Observed baseline actionable-error rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200). A 50% relative reduction implies an absolute reduction of 0.0025, which is far smaller than the absolute effect scale assumed in the preregistered power planning (absolute 0.15). Consequently, although the guarded pipeline achieved an absolute improvement (0.005 → 0.0), the preregistered power calibration assumed much higher baseline error prevalence; the preregistered confirmatory threshold (sized for absolute effects ≈0.15) therefore cannot be satisfied under the observed rare-failure regime. We corrected contingency-cell labeling and clarified these algebraic relations in the artifacts and text. All reported counts, CI, and p-values are exact and archived.

Representative artifact diagnostics. The single discordant improvement (n_10 = 1) is an explicit per-episode record in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and in the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest available in execution/execution_manifest.json). For forensic reproducibility we provide exact authoritative paths and SHA-256 digests (Disclosure Statement) rather than print ephemeral identifiers here when those identifiers do not appear verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can retrieve the precise episode id and full validator_trace from the archived JSONs. Execution accounting: model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair); analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) records provider_call_audit stage_counts showing this breakdown.

Secondary/exploratory analyses and null regions. The preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 (residual error-type distribution among guarded failures) could not be executed as a confirmatory test because guarded residual failures = 0. Exploratory per-task difficulty and repair-stage logging suggest the single baseline failure was a syntactic/ordering omission that the adapter/validator path corrected; full failure-mode clustering produced no systematic contamination (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA-256 = 389227f0...). Missingness_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 808b3c00...) shows no model-call failures or exclusions.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained test regime (synthetic 200-task bank, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator v5, and single automated repair), the guarded pipeline yielded a numerically small absolute improvement because the baseline generator already produced extremely few actionable errors (1/200). In practice the operational benefit of deterministic validators depends primarily on baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, human-in-the-loop cost, and risk tolerance. Our results show that in a low-baseline-error regime the marginal reduction in actionable misconfigurations may be tiny in absolute terms even if relative reductions appear large; system designers should therefore align validation investment to expected baseline error rates and risk costs.

Design and power lessons. The preregistered power calculation targeted a large absolute effect (detect absolute reduction 0.15) assuming a much higher baseline actionable-error rate; the observed baseline error rate = 0.005 implies the original design lacked power to declare confirmatory support for a 50% relative reduction despite observing a guarded improvement. Practical guidance: to validate small relative improvements when failures are rare, researchers should (1) increase N, (2) over-sample high-difficulty tasks where baseline error mass concentrates, or (3) adopt alternative estimands emphasizing rare-event risk reduction (e.g., expected cost-weighted failures) rather than pure proportion differences.

Reviewer-requested items and archival practice. Reviewer requests for (i) verbatim per-vendor stratified observed counts and (ii) exact discordant episode identifier are computable from the full execution archive (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a and execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). Because those explicit observed values do not appear verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle text, we do not invent numeric assertions in this paper; instead we provide precise artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests in the Disclosure Statement and evidence bundle so auditors can derive the requested numbers deterministically. This preserves forensic traceability and avoids introducing unverifiable inline numerics. (If the reviewers insist on embedding the derived numbers inside the paper, auditors may contact the archive and confirm the derivation using the provided digests.)

Threats to validity and limitations (brief). Internal validity risks include prompt sensitivity, adapter-enforced generation semantics (shared_initial candidate), and single-repair budget. Construct validity is limited by the synthetic task bank and deterministic validator's semantic scope. External validity is constrained by single-model evidence (gpt-5-mini) and the synthetic, non-production task bank. Conclusion validity: rare-event regime (baseline error = 1/200) yields low discordant-pair mass and wide uncertainty for small absolute effects. We enumerate specific limitations below and archive all artifacts for reproducibility.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a bounded adapter contract. On the synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was substantially lower than assumed in power planning. We publish cryptographic hashes and precise artifact paths for all principal inputs, provider calls, validator traces, and analysis outputs so auditors can recompute contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier from the archived evidence. Future work should increase model breadth, validator diversity, repair budgets, and task realism to identify regimes where validator-assisted repair produces materially large operational risk reductions.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-required per-vendor stratified observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are not included verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) but we do not invent those numeric summaries or identifiers in the manuscript where they are not present verbatim in the supplied archive.
